kv.memory.gpg-key-validity-policy: GPG attestor enrollment rule, decided by Mark 2026-09-14 (commit 0edf653): a key is enrollable if its secret half is present (sec field 15 != '#', so smartcard serials count as possession) AND field 2 is not 'r'. EXPIRED keys ('e') are deliberately KEPT -- the operator still holds the secret half, only the declared validity window lapsed, and dropping them deletes a capability rather than labelling it (6 of Mark's 17 keys are expired: f5, hp, blackfedora, NTPsec x2, Nemo). Do not 'fix' expired keys into being rejected. Measured fact: revoking a primary marks every uid 'r', so a revoked key is already refused for having no live uid; the sec-level check is kept anyway because nothing in gpg documents that coupling and this is an authorization decision.
kv.memory.presence-gate-multi-audience: FetchJWTSVID presence policy is per-audience and reconciled strictest-wins: the gate folds max(require_presence) over EVERY parsed audience, not audience[0]. Chosen over forbidding multi-audience because proto/spiffe/workload/workload.proto:117-118 makes 'repeated string audience' normative ('the audience(s) the workload intends to authenticate against') and the persona_ extension syntax is per-audience by construction (AudienceExtensions::parse is a pure function of one string; there is no control slot or reserved index). max is commutative and PresenceLevel::None is the least element, so no appended audience at any position can lower the bar. Also: the persona_ query-param namespace is CLOSED -- an unimplemented persona_ param is INVALID_ARGUMENT, never ignored. Resolves persona-5s4b.47 and .71.
kv.memory.report-length: Mark gets flooded by long structured reports. He said so directly: 'you are starting to flood my brain.' When he asks what to work on next, give ONE recommendation in two or three sentences -- no severity tables, no enumerated alternatives, no 'two things to surface'. Save the detailed breakdown for when he asks for it, or put it in the bead where he can read it on his own schedule. This is about volume, not content: the analysis was wanted, the wall of it was not.
kv.memory.watch-never-gives-up: persona watch never terminates on its own -- decided by Mark 2026-09-14, implemented in 76a4a7d. When personad is unreachable it logs to stderr and keeps polling; only Ctrl-C ends it, exiting 0. Chosen over 'exit after N consecutive failures' (a threshold nobody can defend, plus a config knob) and over 'exit on first failure' (a routine daemon restart would kill an interactive watch). The reasoning: the fail-open pattern this repo spent 2026-09-14 removing requires a command to TERMINATE before a shell '&&' gate can be fooled, and watch does not terminate, so the exit-non-zero rule that applies to enroll/fetch-x509/trust-bundle/whoami deliberately does NOT apply here. persona whoami is the health check that answers with an exit code. Do not add a failure threshold to watch.
